page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show weak to poor performance, with read-only large block operations falling into the bottom 10% at 21.24 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also register in the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations fall within the bottom 25%, indicating limited throughput for high-demand transactional workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2.large offers a dedicated CPU allocation without the resource sharing of burstable instances, but its older Intel Xeon architecture yields lower performance-per-resource compared to newer generations. Because it lacks local NVMe storage and exhibits lower benchmark results across computational, memory, and web serving tests, it is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose workloads. Suitable applications include low-traffic web servers, basic development or testing environments, and small-scale background utility tasks that require dedicated CPU cores but do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive computational throughput.
